newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's Export Finance Bank posts 96 profits.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's Export Finance Bank posts 96 profits.

text.p: Jordan Export Finance Bank (EFB) posted 507,984 dinars of operational profits in 1996, its first year of business, and nearly doubled that in the first half year 1997, its chairman said on Tuesday.

"We are building up our balance sheet and the results reflect our competitive advantage in the provision of a comprehensive range of banking and financial services to exporters and major corporations who constitute our core client base," chairman Ali al-Husry told Reuters.
EFB's retained earnings in 1996 were 130,504 dinars in the bank's first financial accounts since it began operations at the start of 1996.
EFB posted 507,984 dinars in operational profits before provisions and taxes in 1996 compared to around 950,000 dinars it made in the first half of 1997, Husry said.
"We have already in the first half of 1997 exceeded handsomely the 1996 results," he added.

The bank's total balance sheet has also soared to 46 million dinars by first half of 1997 from 26 million dinars at end of 1996 as a result of new credit facilities and deposits and money market operations, Husry added.

The bank which has an authorised 20 million dinar capital was the first Jordanian bank to be licensed since the late 1970s. It was also the first which aimed to service Jordan's rapidly growing export finance market.
EFB's first audited balance sheet shows deposits have grown to 13.3 million dinars.
Its lending portfolio grew to 10.7 million dinars, of which nearly 70 percent was in manufacturing and mining and the rest in general trade and transportation services.
The bank last year also participated in four syndicated loans to leading local companies.
The bank's status as a specialist bank which promotes exports allows it to get medium and long term financing from the Central Bank at preferential rates, Husry said.
Its utilisation of a $40 million facility by the World Bank allows it cheaper project finance for its clients, he added.
EFB bank's major shareholders are the country's leading export earners, including Jordan's potash and phosphates industry, the private Hikma Pharmaceutical Company, and Nuqul industrial conglomerate.
